name: create_sql_migration_add_column
description: Writes a backfill migration adding a NOT NULL column to a live table
prompts: schema.sql defines the current users(id, email, name) table, which already holds data in production. Write migration.sql that adds a `status` TEXT column that must end up NOT NULL with every EXISTING row backfilled to 'active'. SQLite can't add a NOT NULL column without a default in one step, so do it as a real migration: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with a temporary nullable form (or a DEFAULT), UPDATE the backfill, and ensure future inserts can't put NULL there (a NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' column achieves this). The migration must be plain SQL statements that run via executescript against a database that already contains rows.

test_setup_files.test_migration.py:
import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.executescript(open('schema.sql').read())
conn.execute("INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('a@x.io', 'Ada')")
conn.execute("INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('b@x.io', 'Bob')")
conn.commit()

conn.executescript(open('migration.sql').read())

rows = conn.execute('SELECT email, status FROM users ORDER BY email').fetchall()
assert rows == [('a@x.io', 'active'), ('b@x.io', 'active')], \
    f'existing rows must be backfilled to active: {rows}'

# future inserts without a status must not become NULL
conn.execute("INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ('c@x.io', 'Cat')")
status = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM users WHERE email = 'c@x.io'").fetchone()[0]
assert status is not None, 'new rows must not get NULL status'

# and the data must have survived the migration
assert conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users').fetchone()[0] == 3
print('PASS')

reference_solution.migration.sql:
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
UPDATE users SET status = 'active' WHERE status IS NULL;

files.migration.sql:
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status TEXT;
UPDATE users SET status = 'active';
